best_for: Linux and Windows users who read PDFs, ebooks and comics in one viewer, and who want to mark up and sign PDFs without paying for an editor.

points.title: One viewer, many formats
points.text: Okular opens PDF, EPub, DjVu and Markdown files, images such as JPEG, PNG, TIFF and WebP, and CBR and CBZ comic archives.

points.title: Notes, highlights and signatures
points.text: You can add inline and pop-up notes, highlight or underline text and type onto a page. It also checks the digital signatures in a PDF, shows whether a file changed after signing, and lets you sign PDFs yourself.

points.title: Free software from KDE
points.text: Okular is part of KDE and released under GPLv2 or later. There is no paid edition.

points.title: On Windows, KDE points to the Store
points.text: KDE recommends the Microsoft Store build because its developers test it and it updates itself; other Windows builds it offers are untested nightlies. The installers here are x64, per-user or for all users. The Windows listing shows 26.11.80 while the Flatpak shows 26.08.3.

points.title: Linux: distro or Flathub
points.text: Most distributions package Okular. The Flathub build is marked verified for KDE, for x64 and Arm64. Ubuntu and Kubuntu packages are built without EPub support.

points.title: No stable Mac release
points.text: KDE offers only untested nightly builds for Intel and Apple silicon Macs, so this page does not list macOS.

points.title: Older versions on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 29 versions. Linux lists only the current Flatpak.
